records.quote:
A single flash--that is A, surely.  Now, then.  How many
did you make it?  Twenty.  So did I.  That should mean T.
records.paraphrase: Holmes decodes flashed signals letter by letter using a numeric cipher.

records.quote:
I don't understand that.  I should say that only a clean-shaven man
could have smoked this.
records.paraphrase: Holmes infers from the cigarette stub that a clean-shaven person smoked it, contradicting the description.

records.quote:
The words are
written with a broad-pointed, violet-tinted pencil of a not unusual
pattern.  You will observe that the paper is torn away at the side here
after the printing was done, so that the 's' of 'soap' is partly gone.
records.paraphrase: Holmes makes detailed observations about the pencil and torn paper to draw inferences.

records.quote:
There seems no other way, and
fortunately we need concern ourselves with the one paper only.  Here
are the Daily Gazette extracts of the last fortnight.
records.paraphrase: Holmes reasons out that communication must occur via newspaper advertisements and reviews the extracts.

records.quote:
from the centre of
his broad, brown, upturned throat there projected the white haft of a
knife driven blade-deep into his body.
records.paraphrase: The body of the giant is found stabbed to death with a knife.

records.quote:
And not a very
obscure cipher, Watson," said he.  "Why, of course, it is Italian!  The
A means that it is addressed to a woman.  'Beware! Beware!  Beware!'
records.paraphrase: Holmes interprets the cipher as Italian, deducing the message and its intended recipient.

records.quote:
We fled together, were married at Bari, and sold my jewels to gain the
money which would take us to America.  This was four years ago, and we
have been in New York ever since.
records.paraphrase: The couple recounts fleeing Italy and relocating to America four years prior.

records.quote:
This other, however, prints 'match' when it should have
been 'matches.'  I can imagine that the word was taken out of a
dictionary, which would give the noun but not the plural.
records.paraphrase: Holmes deduces a substitution of lodgers from the grammatical error suggesting a non-English speaker using a dictionary.

records.quote:
It frightens me, Mr. Holmes.  I
can't sleep for fright.
records.paraphrase: The landlady expresses fear and sleeplessness over the mysterious lodger.

records.quote:
she sprang
into the air with a cry of joy.  Round and round the room she danced,
her hands clapping, her dark eyes gleaming with delighted wonder
records.paraphrase: Emilia Lucca reacts with joyful relief and dancing at the sight of Gorgiano's corpse.

records.quote:
The matches have, of course, been
used to light cigarettes.  That is obvious from the shortness of the
burnt end.  Half the match is consumed in lighting a pipe or cigar.
records.paraphrase: Holmes reasons from physical clues (burnt match length) to deduce their use.

records.quote:
two men came up behind
him, threw a coat over his head, and bundled him into a cab that was
beside the curb.  They drove him an hour, and then opened the door and
shot him out.
records.paraphrase: Mr. Warren is abducted, driven off, and dumped, in a case of mistaken identity.

records.quote:
I caught a glimpse of a dark, beautiful,
horrified face glaring at the narrow opening of the box-room.
records.paraphrase: The hidden lodger reacts with horror upon noticing the observers.

records.quote:
he would signal to me from a
certain window, but when the signals came they were nothing but
warnings
records.paraphrase: The wife explains the arrangement of window-flash signaling as their means of communication.

records.quote:
there was
outlined a fresh track of blood.  The red steps pointed towards us and
led away from an inner room
records.paraphrase: The investigators discover a bloody trail leading to an inner room.

records.quote:
If I take it up I must understand every detail," said he.  "Take time
to consider.  The smallest point may be the most essential.
records.paraphrase: Holmes states a methodical principle of attending to every small detail when investigating.

criteria.rationale: No scientific fact, theory, discovery, natural process, or speculative science is materially represented. The story is a detective narrative relying on ordinary deductive reasoning, not science.

The candle window-flash signaling and newspaper cipher are ordinary period communication methods and a simple substitution code, not an engineered invention or device that speculatively affects the setting. This is a commonplace covert-communication technique, not technology in the SF sense.

The story is set in the contemporary present with only ordinary recent-past backstory (fleeing Italy four years prior, emigration to America). There is no speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement.

No consequences are developed from an identifiable scientific, technological, or speculative premise. The plot extends from a criminal-society premise in a purely realistic mode without extrapolative development of a novum.

Holmes materially drives the plot through systematic observation, inference, and hypothesis-testing: reasoning from the burnt match length, the cigarette stub, the printed 'match' error to infer a substituted lodger, then decoding the flash cipher letter by letter and cross-checking with Watson. This is sustained evidential inference, not mere questioning.
No other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them. The characters are ordinary human immigrants from Italy/America; foreign origin does not qualify.

The events are individual crimes
domestic violence and a single killing, plus a foiled dynamite plot. Though a planned bombing of Castalotte's house is mentioned, it is prevented and remains a discrete criminal act rather than a large-scale catastrophe that is actual, impending, or causally central in a disaster sense.

candidates.description: A window-flash light-signaling system using a numeric substitution cipher (one flash = A, two = B, etc.) by which the hidden husband communicates warnings to his concealed wife, later exploited by Holmes to summon her.

novelty.rationale: Cipher signaling and coded newspaper advertisements are ordinary period devices consistent with the empirical norm of Edwardian London. Nothing about them constitutes a totalizing world-altering difference from the author's implied empirical reality.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The signaling method is presented as a coherent, systematic, nonsupernatural mechanism with an internally consistent code that Holmes reconstructs step by step, but this coherence merely describes a mundane technique.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The signaling drives several key scenes and Holmes's solution, but the overriding narrative logic is the criminal-society revenge plot, not the communication device itself.

estrangement.rationale: The flashing signals create a moment of decoding suspense for the reader, but this is a conventional mystery device, not cognitive estrangement from an altered empirical norm.

candidates.description: Holmes's systematic method of forensic observation and inference, extracting large conclusions from small physical clues (match length, cigarette stub, pencil marks, grammatical errors).

novelty.rationale: Deductive reasoning is a character's skill exercised within an unaltered empirical world; it introduces no totalizing difference from the implied authorial norm.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The method is coherent, systematic, immanent, and explicitly nonsupernatural, but this is analytic technique rather than an imaginary science that changes the world.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: Holmes's method structures the entire investigative narrative, but centrality of an ordinary character skill does not convert it into a novum.

estrangement.rationale: The method impresses but does not estrange the reader from an empirical norm; it operates entirely within the ordinary world.

candidates.description: The Red Circle, a Neapolitan criminal brotherhood allied to the old Carbonari, whose inescapable oaths, blackmail, and murder-by-lot system drive the story's tragedy.

novelty.rationale: A criminal secret society is a realistic social institution within the empirical historical norm (Carbonari, Mafia-type organizations); it is not a totalizing or world-altering difference from the author's implied reality.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The society's organization, funding by blackmail, and enforcement mechanisms are depicted as a coherent, nonsupernatural social system, but a realistic social organization here reflects the world rather than reconstituting it.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The society governs the overriding motive, threat, and resolution of the plot, yet its centrality does not make it a science-fictional novum because it introduces no departure from the empirical norm.

estrangement.rationale: The society generates dread and menace, but this is the ordinary estrangement of crime fiction, not cognitive estrangement from an altered empirical world.
